//: Copy to power.json (gitignored). Each pool maps to smart-plug webhooks — Tasmota, Shelly, or Home Assistant all speak this shape. The collector POSTs the URL on /power/<pool>/<on|off>; Phase 4's drain workloads will call these to unplug the battery pool before a run and restore the 40-70% charge band after.
//read: A pool that also sets read_url + watts_path is METERED: the collector polls it into power_samples and can integrate watt-hours across a job (src/power.ts). watts_path is a path expression, not a vendor name, because Tasmota, Shelly and Kasa each put the number somewhere different. Segments split on '.' and '[…]'; use ["key"] when a key contains a dot, and watts_scale for a plug that reports milliwatts.
//energy_method: REQUIRED for any energy figure — the collector will not guess it. 'plug' means this plug feeds EXACTLY ONE device. 'plug-shared' means several devices sit behind it, and the watt-hours are the POOL's: they must NOT be divided by the number of devices to get a per-device number. A pool that omits this gets no energy figure at all, which is the intended outcome of not knowing how the shelf is wired.
//idle_watts: What this pool draws plugged in and idle — charger bricks, the powered hub, the switch itself. Measure it with the shelf quiet and nothing claimed, then put it here; it is subtracted from every integration. Omit it and the collector estimates it from the pool's own samples and labels the figure as estimated. NOTE: this removes the STANDING load only. A phone on a plug is also charging, and no idle baseline can separate battery charging current from the work — so every result also carries includes_charging, and the dashboard says in words that a charging window's watt-hours include replenishing the battery.
